result:
Compiles successfully.

I wrote `tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/StopWatchAgentTest.java`, covering `StopWatch` and its nested `StopWatch.Split` class purely from the javadoc contract in `api/`:

- Construction (`StopWatch()`, `StopWatch(String)`) and initial state (`isStarted`/`isStopped`/`isSuspended`, `getMessage`)
- `create()` / `createStarted()` factory state
- `start`/`stop`/`suspend`/`resume`/`split`/`unsplit` happy paths and all documented `IllegalStateException` cases (double-start, double-stop, double-suspend, stop/suspend/split/unsplit without a matching prior call, resume without suspend, start after stop without reset)
- `reset()` clearing internal state so accessors throw again and restart succeeds
- Timing accessors and their documented cross-consistency (`getTime`/`getNanoTime`/`getDuration`, `getSplitTime`/`getSplitDuration`/`getSplitNanoTime`, deprecated `getStartTime`/`getStopTime` vs `getStartInstant`/`getStopInstant`), plus `getTime(TimeUnit)` rounding-down behavior
- `formatTime`/`formatSplitTime`/`toString`/`toSplitString` output format (including the documented message prefix)
- `getSplits()` empty-by-default and recording labeled splits
- `StopWatch.Split` constructor, accessors, `toString`, and `equals`/`hashCode`
- `get(Supplier)` / `run(Runnable)` delegation and duration recording

I deliberately skipped `getT(FailableSupplier)`/`runT(FailableRunnable)` since `org.apache.commons.lang3.function.FailableSupplier`/`FailableRunnable` aren't documented anywhere under `api/`, so I'd have been guessing at their exact shape without being allowed to inspect `lib/`.

`./compile.sh` reports `compiled OK`.
